note.text: Tropical savannah is characterised by grasses with varying tree or shrub cover and marked seasonal water limitation. It occurs across parts of Africa, South America and Australia. Cameroon’s broad transition from wetter southern forests towards more seasonal northern landscapes provides local examples. A rainy season supports growth; a dry season constrains water availability. Root systems, leaf shedding and fire responses vary by species. Climate, soil, herbivory, fire and human activity all influence the balance between grasses and woody plants.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to explain seasonal moisture stress and relate grass-tree structure to rainfall fire and land use. Builds on: rainforest structure and the role of moisture. Leads to: savannah soils, wildlife and human activity.

sections.heading: Explain the geography
sections.text: Tropical savannah is characterised by grasses with varying tree or shrub cover and marked seasonal water limitation. It occurs across parts of Africa, South America and Australia. Cameroon’s broad transition from wetter southern forests towards more seasonal northern landscapes provides local examples. A rainy season supports growth; a dry season constrains water availability. Root systems, leaf shedding and fire responses vary by species. Climate, soil, herbivory, fire and human activity all influence the balance between grasses and woody plants.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: A classroom record shows wet months followed by several months with little rain. This helps explain seasonal grass growth and water stress but does not establish an exact vegetation boundary. Some savannah trees shed leaves, while grasses can regrow from protected basal parts. Dense gallery vegetation may follow a watercourse within a more open landscape; a river corridor does not make every surrounding slope rainforest.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Compare distributions across the year rather than annual totals alone. Explain how a plant feature relates to a seasonal constraint, without claiming every species has one adaptation. Do not equate all savannah with recent forest clearing, or all fire with a beneficial outcome. Use regional evidence and acknowledge human modification.

grass cover combined with variable woody vegetation
a feature or behaviour helping plants cope with reduced water availability
interacting climate soil disturbance and grazing influences on vegetation

cards.idea: Explain how the process produces the stated effect.
example: Timing of rain and storage determine dry-season conditions as well as the annual total.
Savannah includes a range of tree and shrub cover.
Reducing active leaf area can reduce water demand, depending on the species.
Vegetation reflects several controls and histories, not a single universal rainfall rule.

questions.prompt: Read the invented monthly rainfall chart. Add the labels above all monthly bars to obtain the annual total in mm; the vertical-axis tick labels are not extra observations.

misconceptions.explain: That is a monthly mean, not the sum for the year.
That is the difference between wettest and driest months, not the annual total.
That multiplies an already millimetre total by ten without a unit conversion.

solution: The annual rainfall of this classroom record is {answer} mm. A real biome classification also needs temperature and other evidence.

right.text: seasonal water stress: a dry period limiting water availability despite a rainy season.
right.explain: This distinction is correct: Timing of rain and storage determine dry-season conditions as well as the annual total. Look for a claim that reverses the process or makes an unsupported generalisation.

right.text: grass-tree mosaic: grass cover combined with variable woody vegetation.
right.explain: This distinction is correct: Savannah includes a range of tree and shrub cover. Look for a claim that reverses the process or makes an unsupported generalisation.

right.text: drought response: a feature or behaviour helping plants cope with reduced water availability.
right.explain: This distinction is correct: Reducing active leaf area can reduce water demand, depending on the species. Look for a claim that reverses the process or makes an unsupported generalisation.

right.text: multiple controls: interacting climate soil disturbance and grazing influences on vegetation.
right.explain: This distinction is correct: Vegetation reflects several controls and histories, not a single universal rainfall rule. Look for a claim that reverses the process or makes an unsupported generalisation.

wrong.text: One wet month guarantees unlimited water throughout the year.
wrong.explain: Timing of rain and storage determine dry-season conditions as well as the annual total.
Savannah includes a range of tree and shrub cover.

wrong.text: Leaf shedding always increases water loss by enlarging the active leaf area.
wrong.explain: Reducing active leaf area can reduce water demand, depending on the species.

wrong.text: Rainfall alone fixes every tree at every site.
wrong.explain: Vegetation reflects several controls and histories, not a single universal rainfall rule.
